messages.subject: Re: export residual matrix
parts: Is there a way to export them as tables that I can use in MS Word?

See the clipboard() function in semTools.  You can paste into Word, but make sure to use a fixed-width font like Courier New or Lucida Console for the numbers to line up.  Better yet, paste into Excel so you can customize the display in each cell, then copy/paste from there into Word (as a table).

messages.subject: Re: export residual matrix
parts: Do you know how I can plot (scatterplots) these standardized residual matrixes in R?

Plot what against what?  If you are comparing the correlation residuals between 2 competing models:

example(cfa)
mod.null <- paste0("x", 1:9, " ~~ foo*x", 1:9)
fit0 <- update(fit, model = mod.null)
(myResiduals1 <- resid(fit, type = "cor"))
(myResiduals0 <- resid(fit0, type = "cor"))
## extract lower triangles
uniqueCorResids1 <- myResiduals1$cor[lower.tri(myResiduals1$cor)]
uniqueCorResids0 <- myResiduals0$cor[lower.tri(myResiduals0$cor)]
plot(x = uniqueCorResids0, y = uniqueCorResids1, xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1),
      xlab = "Null Model", ylab = "Target Model", main = "Competing Model Residuals")
abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = "dotted", col = "grey69")

If you want to visualize the residuals of a single model as differences between observed and model-implied covariances:

example(cfa)
(impliedCor <- lavInspect(fit, "cor.ov"))
impliedVec <- impliedCor [lower.tri(impliedCor )]
(observedCov <- lavInspect(fit, "sampstat"))
observedCor <- cov2cor(observedCov$cov)
observedVec <- observedCor[lower.tri(observedCor)]
plot(x = impliedVec , y = observedVec, xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1),
     main = "Observed vs. Expected Correlations",
     xlab = "Model-Implied", ylab = "Observed")
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = "dotted", col = "grey69")
